headings.title: searchWords
headings.text:
searchWords: readonly (string | RegExp)[] Array of search words.
String search terms are matched literally, unless autoEscape is false
(in which case they are treated as regular expressions, and strings that aren't valid regular expressions are matched literally).
RegExp search terms are used as-is (with their own flags).

headings.title: textToHighlight
headings.text:
textToHighlight: string Text to highlight matches in.
 Browsers collapse whitespace and newlines by default; to preserve them, set the white-space style (e.g. style={{ whiteSpace: "pre-wrap" }}).

headings.title: activeClassName
headings.text:
activeClassName?: string Class name applied to the active match.
 Use along with activeIndex.

headings.title: activeIndex
headings.text:
activeIndex?: number = -1 Index of the match that should be actively highlighted.
 Use along with activeClassName or activeStyle.

headings.title: activeStyle
headings.text:
activeStyle?: CSSProperties Inline styles applied to the active match.
 Use along with activeIndex.

headings.title: autoEscape
headings.text:
autoEscape?: boolean Match string search terms literally (defaults to true).
Set to false to treat them as regular expressions.
(They are compiled without the u flag, so syntax that requires it, such as \p{L}, only works in RegExp search terms.)
 Only set this to false for trusted search terms;
a malicious regular expression can take an extremely long time to run.

headings.title: caseSensitive
headings.text:
caseSensitive?: boolean = false Match string search terms case sensitively.
RegExp search terms are case sensitive unless they have the i flag.

headings.title: className
headings.text: className?: string Class name applied to the outer/wrapper <span>.

headings.title: findChunks
headings.text:
findChunks?: ((options: Required<FindChunksOptions>) => FoundChunk[]) Custom function to search for matching chunks.
This makes it possible to use arbitrary logic when looking for matches.
 It receives the search options (with defaults applied) and returns the start and end index of each range of text to highlight,
along with the searchIndex of the search word that matched it.
Overlapping ranges are combined automatically.
 See the default findChunks function in highlight-words-core for reference.

headings.title: highlightClassName
headings.text:
highlightClassName?: string | Record<string, string> Class name applied to highlighted text,
or an object mapping search term matches to class names.
 Object keys are compared with the matched text first, then with the string search term that matched it
(case insensitively, unless caseSensitive is true).

headings.title: highlightStyle
headings.text: highlightStyle?: CSSProperties = {} Inline styles applied to highlighted text.

headings.title: highlightTag
headings.text:
highlightTag?: string | ComponentType<HighlightTagProps> = "mark" Type of tag to wrap around highlighted matches.
Defaults to mark but can also be a React component (class or function).
 Custom components will receive children, className, highlightIndex, searchIndex, and style props.

headings.title: sanitize
headings.text:
sanitize?: ((text: string) => string) Process each string search word and the text to highlight before comparing (e.g. to remove accents).
Matches always refer to the original text, even if sanitizing changes its length (e.g. "Æ" to "AE").
 Sanitizing should transform characters independently;
if it changes the text, it is applied to each character separately.
RegExp search terms are not sanitized, but they are matched against the sanitized text.

headings.title: unhighlightClassName
headings.text: unhighlightClassName?: string Class name applied to unhighlighted text.

headings.title: unhighlightStyle
headings.text: unhighlightStyle?: CSSProperties Inline styles applied to unhighlighted text.

headings.title: unhighlightTag
headings.text:
unhighlightTag?: string | ComponentType<UnhighlightTagProps> = "span" Type of tag applied to unhighlighted parts of the text.
Defaults to span but can also be a React component (class or function).

text:
Highlights all occurrences of one or more search terms within a larger body of text.
 Highlighted matches are wrapped in a <mark> element by default, and unhighlighted text is wrapped in a <span>.
Both of these can be customized with the highlightTag and unhighlightTag props.
 Any other props (such as title or data-* attributes) are applied to the outer/wrapper <span>, and a ref is forwarded to it.

headings.title: How do I match a pattern instead of a literal word?
Does this package include TypeScript types?
headings.text: Does this package include TypeScript types? Yes. Type definitions are included in the published package, so the @types/react-highlight-words package is no longer needed.

headings.title: Can I match whole words only?
headings.text: Can I match whole words only? Yes. Use the findChunks prop to provide your own matching logic; see the custom matching example.

text: GitHub is the easiest place to look for help, but it's probably not the fastest. This project is maintained by a single developer so there is limited bandwidth for answering questions. I recommend asking questions on Stack Overflow or Reddit to start with. Both sites have active communities who often respond quickly. If you don't find an answer there you can try opening a GitHub issue- but please take a moment first to see if your question has has already been answered before opening a new one.
